passages.text: That night sleep escaped the king; so he ordered the Book of Records, the Chronicles, to be brought in and read to him.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes could not sleep that night.
He was restless.
He gave an order.
He told his servants to bring the Book of Records.
This book was called the Chronicles.
The servants brought the book to the king.
They read the book aloud in front of him.
passages.original: בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא נָדְדָ֖ה שְׁנַ֣ת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְהָבִ֞יא אֶת־ סֵ֤פֶר הַזִּכְרֹנוֹת֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י הַיָּמִ֔ים וַיִּהְי֥וּ נִקְרָאִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: And there it was found recorded that Mordecai had exposed Bigthana and Teresh, two of the eunuchs who guarded the king’s entrance, when they had conspired to assassinate King Xerxes.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew living in Persia.
King Xerxes ruled Persia.
Bigthana and Teresh were two of the king’s eunuchs.
Bigthana and Teresh guarded the entrance to the king’s rooms.
Mordecai discovered a plot.
Bigthana and Teresh planned to kill King Xerxes.
Mordecai told others about the plot.
Someone wrote this event in the royal records.
The record said Mordecai exposed Bigthana and Teresh’s plan to assassinate King Xerxes.
passages.original: וַיִּמָּצֵ֣א כָת֗וּב אֲשֶׁר֩ הִגִּ֨יד מָרְדֳּכַ֜י עַל־ בִּגְתָ֣נָא וָתֶ֗רֶשׁ שְׁנֵי֙ סָרִיסֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מִשֹּׁמְרֵ֖י הַסַּ֑ף אֲשֶׁ֤ר בִּקְשׁוּ֙ לִשְׁלֹ֣חַ יָ֔ד בַּמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרֽוֹשׁ׃

passages.text: The king inquired, “What honor or dignity has been bestowed on Mordecai for this act?” “Nothing has been done for him,” replied the king’s attendants.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes could not sleep that night.
He asked for the Book of Records.
The attendants read the records to him.
The records said that Mordecai had saved the king.
Mordecai had warned about a plot against the king.
Two of the king’s guards had planned to kill the king.
Mordecai had exposed their plan.
King Xerxes asked a question.
He said, “What honor or dignity has been given to Mordecai for this?”
The king’s attendants answered him.
They said, “Nothing has been done for him.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מַֽה־ נַּעֲשָׂ֞ה יְקָ֧ר וּגְדוּלָּ֛ה לְמָרְדֳּכַ֖י עַל־ זֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ נַעֲרֵ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ מְשָׁ֣רְתָ֔יו לֹא־ נַעֲשָׂ֥ה עִמּ֖וֹ דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: “Who is in the court?” the king asked. Now Haman had just entered the outer court of the palace to ask the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows he had prepared for him.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes was in his palace.
King Xerxes asked, “Who is in the court?”
Haman was a high official in the kingdom.
Haman had just entered the outer court of the king’s palace.
Haman came to speak with the king.
Haman wanted to ask the king for permission to hang Mordecai.
Haman had already prepared a gallows for Mordecai.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מִ֣י בֶחָצֵ֑ר וְהָמָ֣ן בָּ֗א לַחֲצַ֤ר בֵּית־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה לֵאמֹ֣ר לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לִתְלוֹת֙ אֶֽת־ מָרְדֳּכַ֔י עַל־ הָעֵ֖ץ אֲשֶׁר־ הֵכִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So the king’s attendants answered him, “Haman is there, standing in the court.” “Bring him in,” ordered the king.
passages.sermon:
The king had attendants who served him.
The king asked his attendants a question.
The attendants answered the king.
They said, “Haman is there.”
They said, “He is standing in the court.”
The king gave an order.
He said, “Bring him in.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ נַעֲרֵ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּ֥ה הָמָ֖ן עֹמֵ֣ד בֶּחָצֵ֑ר וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: Haman entered, and the king asked him, “What should be done for the man whom the king is delighted to honor?” Now Haman thought to himself, “Whom would the king be delighted to honor more than me?”
passages.sermon:
Haman entered the room.
The king spoke to Haman.
The king asked a question.
The king said, “What should be done for the man whom the king wants to honor?”
Haman thought to himself.
Haman believed the king wanted to honor him more than anyone else.
Haman said in his heart, “Who would the king want to honor more than me?”
passages.original: וַיָּבוֹא֮ הָמָן֒ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מַה־ לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת בָּאִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חָפֵ֣ץ בִּיקָר֑וֹ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הָמָן֙ בְּלִבּ֔וֹ לְמִ֞י יַחְפֹּ֥ץ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת יְקָ֖ר יוֹתֵ֥ר מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: And Haman told the king, “For the man whom the king is delighted to honor, have them bring a royal robe that the king himself has worn and a horse on which the king himself has ridden—one with a royal crest placed on its head.
passages.sermon:
Haman spoke to the king.
Haman described what should be done for a man the king wants to honor.
Haman said, "Let them bring a royal robe."
The king himself has worn this robe.
Let them bring a horse.
The king himself has ridden this horse.
Let them place a royal crown on the horse's head."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הָמָ֖ן אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ אִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חָפֵ֥ץ בִּיקָרֽוֹ׃ יָבִ֙יאוּ֙ לְב֣וּשׁ מַלְכ֔וּת אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָֽבַשׁ־ בּ֖וֹ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְס֗וּס אֲשֶׁ֨ר רָכַ֤ב עָלָיו֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר נִתַּ֛ן כֶּ֥תֶר מַלְכ֖וּת בְּרֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: Let the robe and the horse be entrusted to one of the king’s most noble princes. Let them array the man the king wants to honor and parade him on the horse through the city square, proclaiming before him, ‘This is what is done for the man whom the king is delighted to honor!’ ”
passages.sermon:
The king has noble princes.
Give the robe and the horse to one of these noble princes.
The king wants to honor a certain man.
Let the noble prince dress this man in the royal robe.
Let the noble prince place the man on the royal horse.
Lead the man on the horse through the city square.
Call out in front of him.
Say, “This is what is done for the man whom the king delights to honor.”
passages.original: וְנָת֨וֹן הַלְּב֜וּשׁ וְהַסּ֗וּס עַל־ יַד־ אִ֞ישׁ מִשָּׂרֵ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַֽפַּרְתְּמִ֔ים וְהִלְבִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ אֶת־ הָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חָפֵ֣ץ בִּֽיקָר֑וֹ וְהִרְכִּיבֻ֤הוּ עַל־ הַסּוּס֙ בִּרְח֣וֹב הָעִ֔יר וְקָרְא֣וּ לְפָנָ֔יו כָּ֚כָה יֵעָשֶׂ֣ה לָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חָפֵ֥ץ בִּיקָרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “Hurry,” said the king to Haman, “and do just as you proposed. Take the robe and the horse to Mordecai the Jew, who is sitting at the king’s gate. Do not neglect anything that you have suggested.”
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to Haman.
The king gave Haman a command.
The king said, “Hurry.
Take the robe and the horse.
Do everything you have suggested.
Give them to Mordecai the Jew.
Mordecai sits at the king’s gate.
Do not leave out anything you have said.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְהָמָ֗ן מַ֠הֵר קַ֣ח אֶת־ הַלְּב֤וּשׁ וְאֶת־ הַסּוּס֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּ֔רְתָּ וַֽעֲשֵׂה־ כֵן֙ לְמָרְדֳּכַ֣י הַיְּהוּדִ֔י הַיּוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּשַׁ֣עַר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ אַל־ תַּפֵּ֣ל דָּבָ֔ר מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתָּ׃

passages.text: So Haman took the robe and the horse, arrayed Mordecai, and paraded him through the city square, crying out before him, “This is what is done for the man whom the king is delighted to honor!”
passages.sermon:
Haman was a high official in the Persian Empire.
Mordecai was a Jew who sat at the king’s gate.
The king wanted to honor Mordecai.
Haman took the royal robe and the horse.
Haman put the robe on Mordecai.
Haman set Mordecai on the king’s horse.
Haman led Mordecai through the city square.
Haman walked in front of Mordecai.
Haman called out, “This is what is done for the man whom the king delights to honor.”
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֤ח הָמָן֙ אֶת־ הַלְּב֣וּשׁ וְאֶת־ הַסּ֔וּס וַיַּלְבֵּ֖שׁ אֶֽת־ מָרְדֳּכָ֑י וַיַּרְכִּיבֵ֙הוּ֙ בִּרְח֣וֹב הָעִ֔יר וַיִּקְרָ֣א לְפָנָ֔יו כָּ֚כָה יֵעָשֶׂ֣ה לָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חָפֵ֥ץ בִּיקָרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then Mordecai returned to the king’s gate. But Haman rushed home, with his head covered in grief.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew.
Mordecai sat at the king’s gate.
Mordecai returned to the king’s gate.
Haman was an official of the king.
Haman rushed to his house.
Haman felt grief.
Haman covered his head.
passages.original: וַיָּ֥שָׁב מָרְדֳּכַ֖י אֶל־ שַׁ֣עַר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְהָמָן֙ נִדְחַ֣ף אֶל־ בֵּית֔וֹ אָבֵ֖ל וַחֲפ֥וּי רֹֽאשׁ׃

passages.text: Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened. His advisers and his wife Zeresh said to him, “Since Mordecai, before whom your downfall has begun, is Jewish, you will not prevail against him—for surely you will fall before him.”
passages.sermon:
Haman was a high official in the Persian Empire.
Haman had a wife named Zeresh.
Haman had many friends.
Haman had advisers.
Mordecai was a Jew.
Mordecai had begun to cause Haman’s downfall.
Haman told Zeresh everything that had happened to him.
Haman told all his friends everything that had happened to him.
Haman’s advisers spoke to him.
Zeresh, Haman’s wife, also spoke to him.
They said, “Mordecai is from the Jewish people.”
They said, “You have begun to fall before Mordecai.”
They said, “You will not be able to overcome Mordecai.”
They said, “You will surely fall before Mordecai.”
passages.original: וַיְסַפֵּ֨ר הָמָ֜ן לְזֶ֤רֶשׁ אִשְׁתּוֹ֙ וּלְכָל־ אֹ֣הֲבָ֔יו אֵ֖ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָרָ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֩אמְרוּ֩ ל֨וֹ חֲכָמָ֜יו וְזֶ֣רֶשׁ אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ אִ֣ם מִזֶּ֣רַע הַיְּהוּדִ֡ים מָרְדֳּכַ֞י אֲשֶׁר֩ הַחִלּ֨וֹתָ לִנְפֹּ֤ל לְפָנָיו֙ לֹא־ תוּכַ֣ל ל֔וֹ כִּֽי־ נָפ֥וֹל תִּפּ֖וֹל לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: While they were still speaking with Haman, the king’s eunuchs arrived and rushed him to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
passages.sermon:
Haman was talking with his wife and friends.
The king’s eunuchs arrived.
The eunuchs hurried Haman.
They took Haman to the banquet.
Esther had prepared the banquet.
passages.original: עוֹדָם֙ מְדַבְּרִ֣ים עִמּ֔וֹ וְסָרִיסֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הִגִּ֑יעוּ וַיַּבְהִ֙לוּ֙ לְהָבִ֣יא אֶת־ הָמָ֔ן אֶל־ הַמִּשְׁתֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־ עָשְׂתָ֥ה אֶסְתֵּֽר׃
